answer: Give every new identity a costly proof-of-work kernel: before an agent can join the nebula of traders, it must burn real compute solving a puzzle tied to its public key, a cost no shortcut can fake. One identity is cheap; ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand puzzles, so a sybil farmer's budget caps the size of its army at the zenith of what it can afford. Honest agents pay the price once, while attackers pay it per fake, every time.
